discoveries:
- The `git log` header of a merge repeats once per non-empty diff. A diff that is empty against a parent prints no header, so a merge that is empty against every parent is not listed and is read as before.
- Pathspec `-- '*.md'` on the `git log` pass made it slower (16 s against 11.6 s) and drops commits, so I did not use it.
- A merge that is the change counts its own owner trailer as the approval. The old code agreed (parity), so an owner merge that brings an agent-set decision is approved. My first expectation was wrong and I fixed the scenario.
- The opt-in rule deselects some parametrized cases silently. Without `GOV_TESTS_OPTIN=lifted,breadth`, 37 of my cases were deselected.

risks:
- `_changes` now returns `(parents tuple, frozenset)` for one-parent commits (it was `(parent, frozenset)`) and also lists merges. The only users I found are `_approved` and my own test. An acceptance test that pins the old shape would fail, but none under W2-45 failed. I could not read the test designer's new cases, which are merged later.
- On this loaded machine the merge case is 19 to 24 s, with 19.3 s only at lower load. It is well under 60 s but not clearly under the 20 s aim.

lessons:
- Check the opt-in deselection count before trusting "N passed".
- The profile showed the cost moved from the walk to the single git pass and to the merges that legitimately bring the file. Further speed-up would need `read_merge`, in `containment_merge`, which is outside my paths.
